newsitem.title: INDIA: Mahathir asks India to use Malaysia as gateway.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir asks India to use Malaysia as gateway.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Friday his country could be an economic gateway for India to gain access to other Southeast Asian markets.

"Malaysia can offer India a gateway to Southeast Asia," Mahathir, on a three-day visit to India, told businessmen at a meeting organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII). A delegation of senior businessmen is accompanying him.

Mahathir said he urged Malaysian businessmen to seek joint ventures with industries in other developing countries and listed several areas in which his country had acquired expertise in recent years of high growth.
They included highway construction, power supply, oil exploration, housing, telecommunications, hotels and tourism.

"Malaysia has always offered itself as a base to penetrate the ASEAN (Association of South East Asian Nations) markets," he said, in response to a question on whether Kuala Lumpur would offer an opportunity for India to gain access to markets in Vietnam and Laos.

India was the fifth largest foreign investor in Malaysia, and Malaysia was among the top 10 investors in India, Mahathir said, adding that recent agreements to avoid double taxation and guarantee the safety of investments would promote business further.
"Our two governments continue to strengthen institutional arrangements to the private sectors of both countries to undertake business on a sustained basis," Mahathir said.
Malaysia's Tetracon Engineering Sdn Bhd signed three memoranda of understanding (MOUs) with Indian companies in power generation, infrastructure management and engineering consultancy on Friday.
Two other MOUs were also signed during Mahathir's visit, which is scheduled to conclude on Sunday.
